cvEn:
Edmond Harosh, son of Anet and Yehuda, was born on the 3rd of Iyar 5698 (4 May 1938) in Casablanca, Morocco. While still abroad he completed his primary schooling and also attended secondary school there. The family immigrated to Israel in 1961. Because of his sporting inclinations, he was a member of a sports club. He worked as a dispatcher at the Dead Sea works, and that was how he earned his living. He was drafted into the IDF in February 1962, and upon his discharge he was called up for reserve duty.

When the Six-Day War broke out, he was called to the flag and fought as an armored corps soldier, out of loyalty to his role and to his comrades. On the first day of its battles, the 26th of Iyar 5727 (5 June 1967), he fell in the battle fought at Al-Jiradi in Sinai. He was brought for burial in the Bari Emergency Military Cemetery, and after some time he was reinterred in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem.

His name is commemorated in the booklet "Lezikhram" published by the Dimona municipality. He is also remembered in "Niv," published by the Dead Sea Works.
